financials_interim.notes: INSURER field mapping (life insurer, single-entity filing -- no separate Group/Company columns anywhere in this filing, unlike RHL/KPHL/VLL; stored as one GROUP-basis row per project convention, since 25% associate First Capital Holdings PLC is equity-accounted, not consolidated -- there is no subsidiary structure to consolidate). Uses the SIX-MONTH CUMULATIVE 'For the Period Ended 30 June' statements (p.2-3, cash flow p.7-8), not the 'For Three Months Ended 30 June' Q2-only statements also disclosed on p.5-6, consistent with how AAIC (Softlogic Life) was entered in this DB. revenue = the filing's own 'Net Income' subtotal (6,322,567), which decomposes as Net premium after reinsurance cession (4,901,557 = GWP 5,111,720 - Premium Ceded to Reinsurers 210,162) + Total Other Revenue (1,421,010, itself = Fee/Commission Income 9,069 + Investment Income 1,621,793 + Realised Gains/(Loss) 41,187 + Fair Value Gains/(Losses) -334,862 + Other Operating Revenue 83,823) -- i.e. materially the task's prescribed 'Net Earned Premium + Investment Income' concept, using the insurer's own disclosed subtotal rather than a reconstruction. GWP itself (Note 15, 5,111,720 vs 3,769,137 LY, +35.6%) is the more conventional insurer top-line and is cited here for context but NOT stored as 'revenue' to stay faithful to the filing's own 'Net Income' framing. operating_profit left BLANK: no distinct pre-finance-cost/pre-tax subtotal is disclosed -- Admin expenses (901,043) and Finance Cost (110,874) are combined into a single 'Total Other Expenses' (1,011,917) line, and the P&L proceeds straight from that to Share of Associate result to PBT, with no intermediate 'operating profit' line. finance_costs = the filing's own separately-itemised 'Finance Cost' figure within Total Other Expenses (110,874 vs 135,209 LY) -- this one line IS cleanly disclosed even though operating_profit is not. finance_income left blank: Investment Income (1,621,793) is presented as part of insurance revenue (within Total Other Revenue), not as a distinct non-insurance 'finance income' line comparable to a general company's -- consistent with the AAIC precedent. gross_profit/cost_of_sales left blank (no COGS concept for an insurer). minority_interest left blank: 100% shareholder-owned, no NCI. Balance sheet is liquidity-ordered (no current/non-current split), so current_assets/current_liabilities are left blank, matching AAIC precedent. inventory/trade_receivables/trade_payables left blank per the task's insurer guidance: the closest analogues are Premium Receivables (498,968) and Reinsurance Receivable (60,494) on the asset side, and Reinsurance Creditors (149,285) and Other Liabilities (2,668,298) on the liability side -- all insurance-specific items, not generic trade receivables/payables, and are therefore excluded from those fields rather than force-mapped. cash_and_equivalents = balance sheet 'Cash and cash equivalents' (790,469); the cash flow statement's own reconciliation nets this against a Rs.110,781k bank overdraft to a narrower Rs.679,688k 'Net Cash and Cash Equivalents' figure. short_term_borrowings = Bank Overdraft (110,781) -- the only short-term-debt-like balance-sheet item disclosed (no separate 'current portion of long-term borrowings' line exists), consistent with the GLAS precedent in this DB of using the overdraft balance when no dedicated short-term-borrowings line exists. long_term_borrowings = 'Long Term Borrowings' (1,351,592) as disclosed. shares_in_issue = 679,578,459 (Note 21 twenty-largest-shareholders total; Note 19 gives the same figure rounded to 679,578 thousand). IMPORTANT: ordinary shares were SUBDIVIDED 3x on 9 April 2026 (226,526,153 to 679,578,459 per Note 19 footnote), i.e. mid-way through this H1 period; the filing's 'Restated Basic Earning per Share' figures (0.19 for H1 2026, 1.94 for H1 2025) are both computed on the POST-subdivision share count (679,578,459) applied retrospectively to both periods for comparability -- verified: PAT 129,585,000 / 679,578,459 = 0.1907, rounds to the printed 0.19. eps_basic here stores this restated figure as printed. MATERIAL ONE-OFF ITEM driving the profit decline: 'Share of Profit/(Loss) of Equity Accounted Investee' (the 25% stake in First Capital Holdings PLC) swung from a Rs.659,994k PROFIT contribution in H1 2025 to a Rs.288,917k LOSS contribution in H1 2026 -- a Rs.948,911k unfavourable swing, larger in magnitude than the entire PBT decline (Rs.1,237,394k). Full PBT bridge (verified to tie exactly for both periods): Net Income change +341,704 (favourable: strong premium growth of +35.4% net, Rs.4,901,557 vs Rs.3,619,513, partly offset by a Rs.940,340k decline in Total Other Revenue -- itself the net of a Rs.1,722,803k collapse in Realised Gains, Rs.41,187 vs Rs.1,763,990, and a Rs.980,374k improvement in Fair Value Gains/Losses, -334,862 vs -1,315,236) - Total Benefits/Claims/Acquisition Cost change -482,770 (unfavourable: Net Benefits and Claims Paid rose 41.1% to Rs.2,240,670k) - Total Other Expenses change -147,417 (unfavourable: Admin Expenses rose 23.6% to Rs.901,043k) - Associate swing -948,911 (as above, unfavourable) = -1,237,394 net change in PBT (839,792,597 error-check n/a; JINS PBT 271,483 vs 1,508,877 LY, -82.0%). Without the associate swing alone, PBT would have RISEN materially rather than falling 82%. This is a genuinely non-operating, investee-level swing (First Capital Holdings' own results, not Janashakthi's insurance operations) and should not be read as deterioration in the core life insurance book, whose premium growth (+35.6% GWP) was in fact strong. Identity checks: PBT-tax=PAT ties exactly (271,483-141,898=129,585); total_assets=total_liab+total_equity ties exactly (41,144,096=24,373,552+16,770,544).

thesis.thesis_text: Janashakthi Insurance PLC is a regulated Sri Lankan life insurer with a 25%-owned equity-accounted associate stake in First Capital Holdings PLC. For H1 2026 (six months ended 30 June 2026), Group PBT collapsed 82.0% YoY to Rs.271,483k and PAT fell 90.2% to Rs.129,585k, but this is not a deterioration in the core insurance business: Gross Written Premium grew a healthy 35.6% YoY to Rs.5,111,720k, and the entire PBT decline is explained by First Capital Holdings' equity-accounted result swinging from a Rs.659,994k profit contribution to a Rs.288,917k loss contribution (a Rs.948,911k swing exceeding the whole PBT decline), compounded by a Rs.1,722,803k fall in Realised Gains on the investment portfolio. Net Benefits and Claims did rise faster than premium growth (+41.1% vs +35.4%), a genuine cost pressure worth watching separately. At ~1.71x P/B with an unusable P/E on this depressed base and no dividend data on file, valuation is not attractive on reported figures despite the healthy underlying premium growth -- the concentration risk in a single, volatile external associate is the key overhang on this thesis (Interim Financial Statements, source_doc_id 52661, p.2-3, Note 15).
thesis.gaps_note: Macro & Industry Outlook (10% weight) unavailable -- no Sri Lankan insurance-penetration, interest-rate, or capital-markets data source exists in this project; the remaining five pillars are renormalized to sum to 100% (Financial Quality 33.3%, Growth 22.2%, Valuation 22.2%, Business Quality 16.7%, Governance & Risk 5.6%). Confidence is limited: only ONE interim (H1 cumulative) period is on file (first financial_statements entry for JINS in this DB, no QoQ split available), no dividend data exists, and no qualitative explanation is given anywhere in the filing for why First Capital Holdings' own equity-accounted result swung so sharply -- that swing being external to JINS's own operations and outside this filing's scope.

financial_quality.rationale: H1 2026 (six months ended 30 June 2026) Group PBT collapsed 82.0% YoY to Rs.271,483k (H1 2025: Rs.1,508,877k) and PAT fell 90.2% to Rs.129,585k -- but this headline collapse decomposes almost entirely into a single non-underwriting item: Share of Profit/(Loss) of Equity Accounted Investee (First Capital Holdings PLC, 25%-owned associate) swung from a Rs.659,994k PROFIT contribution in H1 2025 to a Rs.288,917k LOSS contribution in H1 2026 -- a Rs.948,911k unfavourable swing, LARGER than the entire Rs.1,237,394k PBT decline. Total liabilities/equity of 1.45x (24,373,552/16,770,544) is unremarkable for an insurer carrying technical reserves. Net Benefits and Claims rose 41.1% YoY to Rs.2,240,670k, a genuine cost pressure worth monitoring separately from the associate-driven collapse. ROE this half (PAT/equity) was just 0.77%, materially depressed by the one-off associate swing rather than reflecting the underlying insurance book's health.

growth_outlook.rationale: Gross Written Premium (Note 15) grew a healthy 35.6% YoY to Rs.5,111,720k (H1 2025: Rs.3,769,137k), and Net premium after reinsurance cession grew 35.4% to Rs.4,901,557k -- genuine, strong core underwriting growth that is NOT the source of the profit collapse. However, Net Benefits and Claims grew faster in relative terms within the cost base (+41.1% to Rs.2,240,670k) and Underwriting & Net Acquisition Cost rose 29.2% to Rs.1,409,650k, both outpacing premium growth on the cost side -- worth watching for claims-experience deterioration even though the current-period PBT collapse is dominated by the First Capital Holdings associate swing (Rs.948,911k) and a Rs.1,722,803k fall in Realised Gains on the investment portfolio (partly offset by a Rs.980,374k improvement in Fair Value Gains/Losses), not by underwriting itself.

valuation.rationale: At Rs.42.20 (2026-08-31), P/E based on this half's depressed EPS (Rs.0.19 x2 annualised = Rs.0.38) implies an unusable ~111x multiple, entirely a function of the one-off associate/investment swings documented above rather than a meaningful earnings run-rate. Book value of ~Rs.24.68/share (total equity Rs.16,770,544k / 679,578,459 shares) implies a P/B of ~1.71x -- not cheap for an insurer, especially set against a half where reported profitability was depressed by non-recurring items. No dividend data is on file, so no yield support is available. The combination of an unreliable P/E and a rich P/B, without a clean normalised-earnings figure to re-rate against, argues for caution on valuation despite the healthy underlying premium growth.

business_quality.rationale: Janashakthi Insurance PLC (Insurance sector) is a regulated life insurer with a single-entity filing structure (no consolidated subsidiaries) and a material 25%-owned equity-accounted associate stake in First Capital Holdings PLC, a financial-services group. This associate concentration is a genuine business-quality and governance consideration flagged by the data: First Capital's own results swinging from a Rs.659,994k profit contribution to a Rs.288,917k loss contribution shows JINS's reported earnings are meaningfully exposed to a single external financial-services entity's performance, separate from and larger in magnitude than JINS's own core insurance profitability swings this half. The core life-insurance underwriting business itself, evidenced by 35.6% GWP growth, appears healthy.

governance_risk.rationale: JINS is regulated by the Insurance Regulatory Commission of Sri Lanka (IRCSL) by virtue of being a licensed insurer, a governance positive. No circulars/disclosures feed exists to independently verify board or ownership changes. The associate concentration risk (First Capital Holdings PLC) is a genuine risk factor: no qualitative commentary in this filing explains WHY First Capital's equity-accounted result swung so sharply, since that is external to JINS's own filing. Ordinary shares were subdivided 3x on 9 April 2026 mid-period, correctly reflected on a restated basis in the reported EPS figures for both periods.

key_reasons: H1 2026 Group PBT collapsed 82.0% YoY to Rs.271,483k and PAT fell 90.2% to Rs.129,585k, but this is NOT a core-underwriting story: Gross Written Premium grew a healthy 35.6% YoY to Rs.5,111,720k, and the entire PBT decline is explained by the First Capital Holdings PLC (25%-owned associate) equity-accounted result swinging from a Rs.659,994k profit contribution to a Rs.288,917k loss contribution -- a Rs.948,911k swing larger than the whole PBT decline

A secondary drag was a Rs.1,722,803k collapse in Realised Gains on the investment portfolio, partly offset by a Rs.980,374k improvement in Fair Value Gains/Losses -- an investment-portfolio timing effect, also not a core-underwriting issue

Valuation is not attractive on reported figures (P/E unusable due to the depressed base, ~1.71x P/B) despite the healthy premium growth, since no clean normalised-earnings figure exists in this data to re-rate the multiples against
watch_factors: The First Capital Holdings PLC associate stake is a concentrated, external, non-insurance risk factor now responsible for the majority of JINS's reported profit volatility -- its own drivers are outside this filing and cannot be independently assessed

Net Benefits and Claims rose 41.1% YoY to Rs.2,240,670k, faster than the 35.4% net premium growth -- worth monitoring for genuine claims-experience deterioration separate from the associate/investment-driven headline collapse
No dividend data is on file for JINS in this database, removing a potential valuation support/signal that exists for several peers

horizon_notes.6m: Next interim filing will show whether the First Capital Holdings associate result reverts toward its prior profit-contributing pattern or continues as a drag, and whether GWP growth (currently 35.6%) is sustained.
horizon_notes.1y: If claims growth (41.1% this half) continues to outpace premium growth, underwriting margin could come under genuine pressure even with the associate swing excluded -- worth tracking on a normalised basis.
horizon_notes.3y: Thesis depends on whether JINS's core life-insurance underwriting can keep compounding at a mid-30s percentage GWP growth rate while the First Capital Holdings associate stake's earnings volatility is managed or reduced.
horizon_notes.5y: No macro/industry data source in this project to assess a multi-year Sri Lankan insurance-penetration or interest-rate cycle relevant to JINS's investment portfolio and underwriting margins.

interim_updates.note_text: Janashakthi Insurance PLC (JINS) reported Net Income (the filing's own revenue subtotal = Net Earned Premium after reinsurance cession + Total Other Revenue) of Rs.6,322.57mn for the six months ended 30 June 2026, +5.7% YoY (H1 2025: Rs.5,980.86mn), but Profit before Taxation collapsed 82.0% YoY to Rs.271.48mn (H1 2025: Rs.1,508.88mn) and Profit for the Period fell 90.2% to Rs.129.59mn (H1 2025: Rs.1,318.22mn); Basic EPS fell to Rs.0.19 from Rs.1.94. The PBT decline of Rs.1,237.39mn decomposes fully and exactly into four line-item changes (verified by summation): (1) Share of Profit/(Loss) of Equity Accounted Investee (First Capital Holdings PLC, 25%-owned associate) swung from a Rs.659.99mn PROFIT contribution in H1 2025 to a Rs.288.92mn LOSS contribution in H1 2026, a Rs.948.91mn negative swing -- this single line is LARGER than the entire PBT decline and is the dominant driver; (2) Net Benefits and Claims (Total Benefits, Claims and Net Acquisition Cost) rose 11.3% to Rs.4,750.25mn from Rs.4,267.48mn, a Rs.482.77mn additional cost (within this, Net Benefits and Claims specifically rose 41.1% to Rs.2,240.67mn from Rs.1,588.55mn, and Underwriting & Net Acquisition Cost rose 29.2% to Rs.1,409.65mn from Rs.1,091.64mn); (3) Total Other Expenses (Admin + Finance Cost) rose 17.1% to Rs.1,011.92mn from Rs.864.50mn, a Rs.147.42mn additional cost (within this, Operating and Administrative Expenses rose 23.6% to Rs.901.04mn from Rs.729.29mn, while Finance Cost fell 18.0% to Rs.110.87mn from Rs.135.21mn); (4) Net Income itself grew Rs.341.70mn (the +5.7% noted above), a partial offset. Within Net Income's own composition, two large offsetting swings occurred: Realised Gains/(Loss) collapsed 97.7% to Rs.41.19mn from Rs.1,763.99mn (a Rs.1,722.80mn negative swing), while Fair Value Gains/(Losses) improved to a smaller Rs.334.86mn LOSS from a Rs.1,315.24mn LOSS a year earlier (a Rs.980.37mn positive swing) -- these two investment-related items net to roughly a Rs.742.43mn drag within Other Revenue, alongside Investment Income itself falling 11.5% to Rs.1,621.79mn from Rs.1,832.04mn; Total Other Revenue fell 39.8% to Rs.1,421.01mn from Rs.2,361.35mn as a result. This investment-income softness was more than offset at the Net Income line by Net premium after reinsurance cession growing 35.4% to Rs.4,901.56mn from Rs.3,619.51mn (Gross Written Premium itself, Note 15, rose 35.6% to Rs.5,111.72mn from Rs.3,769.14mn), the insurer's core underlying premium growth. Income Tax Expense fell 25.6% YoY to Rs.141.90mn (H1 2025: Rs.190.65mn), broadly tracking the much smaller pretax profit base. In summary: JINS's headline PBT/PAT collapse is NOT a core-underwriting story (GWP grew a healthy 35.6% and net premium 35.4%) but is driven first by the First Capital Holdings associate result swinging from a Rs.659.99mn contribution to a Rs.288.92mn drag (the single largest factor, exceeding the entire PBT decline on its own), and second by a Rs.1,722.80mn fall in Realised Gains on the investment portfolio (largely offset by a smaller Fair Value loss than the prior year) and a rise in claims/underwriting costs.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is JINS's first financial_statements/interim_updates entry in this DB (the filing itself discloses cumulative six-month 'For the Period Ended 30 June' figures, and the separately-disclosed 'For Three Months Ended 30 June' Q2-only statements on p.5-6 were not used, consistent with the AAIC/Softlogic Life precedent in this DB, so no Q1-2026-only figure is available here to derive a QoQ split without re-reading those pages). Genuine filing-level gaps: (1) no qualitative commentary explains WHY First Capital Holdings PLC's equity-accounted result swung from a Rs.659.99mn profit contribution to a Rs.288.92mn loss contribution -- this is the single largest driver of JINS's own PBT decline but the underlying cause (First Capital's own trading/investment performance) is external to this filing and not disclosed within it; (2) no breakdown is given of which asset classes drove the Rs.1,722.80mn fall in Realised Gains or the improvement in Fair Value Gains/(Losses) (equity vs. government securities vs. corporate debt); (3) no rationale is given for the 41.1% rise in Net Benefits and Claims (Rs.1,588.55mn to Rs.2,240.67mn) -- claims-experience commentary is absent from the interim filing; (4) operating_profit is genuinely NOT DISCLOSED as a distinct filing subtotal (Admin expenses and Finance Cost are combined into 'Total Other Expenses' with no intermediate operating-profit line before Share of Associate result and PBT) -- left blank in financial_statements and omitted from yoy_json for that reason, not a data gap in this narrative process itself.
interim_updates.takeaway: JINS's 82.0% PBT and 90.2% PAT collapse is driven almost entirely by two non-underwriting items: the First Capital Holdings associate swinging from a Rs.659.99mn profit contribution to a Rs.288.92mn loss contribution (a Rs.948.91mn swing exceeding the entire PBT decline), and a Rs.1,722.80mn fall in Realised Gains on the investment book. Core insurance operations were actually healthy in the period -- Gross Written Premium grew 35.6% YoY -- so the headline profit collapse should be read as an investment-portfolio and associate-earnings story, not a deterioration in the underlying insurance business, though the 41.1% rise in Net Benefits and Claims is a genuine cost pressure worth monitoring alongside claims experience commentary that this filing does not provide.

yoy.label: Restated Basic Earnings per Share, Rs. (Group)

operational_highlights: Share of Profit/(Loss) of Equity Accounted Investee (First Capital Holdings PLC, 25%-owned) swung from a Rs.659.99mn PROFIT contribution to a Rs.288.92mn LOSS contribution YoY -- a Rs.948.91mn negative swing, larger than the entire Rs.1,237.39mn PBT decline on its own.

Realised Gains/(Loss) on investments collapsed 97.7% to Rs.41.19mn from Rs.1,763.99mn PY (Rs.1,722.80mn swing), partly offset by Fair Value Gains/(Losses) improving to a Rs.334.86mn loss from a Rs.1,315.24mn loss PY (Rs.980.37mn favourable swing); net effect roughly Rs.742.43mn negative within Other Revenue.

Net premium after reinsurance cession grew 35.4% YoY to Rs.4,901.56mn (Gross Written Premium, Note 15, +35.6% to Rs.5,111.72mn from Rs.3,769.14mn) -- healthy core underwriting growth, masked at the PBT line by the associate and investment-portfolio swings above.

Net Benefits and Claims rose 41.1% YoY to Rs.2,240.67mn (H1 2025: Rs.1,588.55mn); Underwriting & Net Acquisition Cost rose 29.2% to Rs.1,409.65mn; Operating and Administrative Expenses rose 23.6% to Rs.901.04mn.
key_drivers: First Capital Holdings PLC (25%-owned associate) equity-accounted result swinging from a Rs.659.99mn profit to a Rs.288.92mn loss (Rs.948.91mn negative swing) is the single largest driver of the 82.0% PBT decline -- larger in magnitude than the entire PBT fall.

Realised Gains on the investment portfolio falling Rs.1,722.80mn YoY (Rs.1,763.99mn to Rs.41.19mn) is a second major drag, only partly offset by a Rs.980.37mn favourable swing in Fair Value Gains/(Losses).

Core insurance underwriting was healthy and NOT a driver of the decline: Gross Written Premium grew 35.6% YoY to Rs.5,111.72mn, more than offsetting the 41.1% rise in Net Benefits and Claims at the revenue (Net Income) line.
